comments.author: Alexander Terp
comments.body:
Bigger than a transient. Measured while running the app against a real daemon: a subscription that has just bootstrapped replays layout events, so a tab walks backwards through arrangements it had minutes ago - a three-pane tab published one pane, then two, then three again, each as though it were current. The transient during a split is the same behavior on a shorter timescale.

The core now withholds any tree that disagrees with its tab's pane list, which covers both, but the probe should record it so docs/observations/herdr-0.8.0.md can cite a transcript rather than a test log. Two scenarios: split a two-pane tab and capture the tree in between, and open a subscription against an already-split tab and capture what it replays.

creator: Alexander Terp
description:
Splitting a two-pane tab publishes a layout naming only one pane before publishing the settled tree. Composition now treats the pane list as the authority on what exists and the tree as an ordering only (corpus/conformance/composition.json, 'a tree that has not caught up does not move the keyboard'), which is the right rule regardless - but the herdr behavior behind it was observed in a test log rather than recorded.

Add it to tools/herdr-probe's layout scenario: split a two-pane tab with a subscription open, capture every layout_updated in order, and write the sequence into corpus/herdr-0.8.0/layout/. Then docs/observations/herdr-0.8.0.md section 13 can state it with a citation instead of the claim resting on a comment.

Worth doing because the same shape probably applies to close and move, and because anything else that reads a tree as evidence will hit it too.
title: 🔬 Record herdr's transient one-pane tree during a split
